tool.name: TrimN
tool.description: removes fake cut sites and trims Ns
tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What it does**
TrimNs is part of the VGP pipeline, and is made of a series of python scripts which trim off large stretches of N bases and to remove fake cut sites that sometimes get inserted at the end of bionano hybrid scaffolds.
Underlying software source documentation: - trimns_vgp vgp-assembly-01ae8b83dbbc4ba77f8d6cd289999211e642e143/pipeline/bionano/trimNs/README.md: ## Details of each script ### remove_fake_cut_sites_DNAnexus.py This script removes the spurious BioNano cut sites that are inserted into gaps in some assemblies, replacing them with Ns. ``` Usage: python3 remove_fake_cut_sites_DNAnexus.py <input.fa> <output.fa> <output.log> ``` - trimns_vgp vgp-assembly-01ae8b83dbbc4ba77f8d6cd289999211e642e143/pipeline/bionano/trimNs/README.md: into gaps in some assemblies, replacing them with Ns. ``` Usage: python3 remove_fake_cut_sites_DNAnexus.py <input.fa> <output.fa> <output.log> ``` Where: * `input.fa` is the input FASTA file * `output.fa` is the output with any cut sites in the middle of a run of - trimns_vgp vgp-assembly-01ae8b83dbbc4ba77f8d6cd289999211e642e143/pipeline/bionano/trimNs/README.md: ### trim_Ns_DNAnexus.py This identifies runs of Ns near the ends of sequences (despite the name of the script, it only identifies these regions; it does not actually trim them). More specifically, it identifies runs of Ns that are *directly* at the ends of scaffolds, but it also removes runs of Ns that are very near the ends of scaffolds (it looks at the 5 kb window at each end of the scaffold, and if more than 3 kb of that is Ns, it slides the - trimns_vgp vgp-assembly-01ae8b83dbbc4ba77f8d6cd289999211e642e143/pipeline/bionano/trimNs/README.md: takes this into account. ``` Usage: python3 trim_Ns_DNAnexus.py <input.fa> <output.list> ``` Where: * `input.fa` is the input FASTA file * `output.list` is a record of the locations for trimming
